LMPC.title: Hirsch and Chatin lead LMPC from start to finish
LMPC.dek: Gary Hirsch and Paul Loup Chatin won LMPC from pole, a lap clear of Anthony Pons and Soheil Ayari, in a class made up of three Team Endurance Challenge Orecas.

chapters.title: A one-team class
text: LMPC reached Imola as a class run by a single team. Team Endurance Challenge entered all three Formula Le Mans Oreca 09s: the #47 for Alex Loan and Matthieu Lecuyer, the #48 for Anthony Pons and Soheil Ayari and the #49 for Paul Loup Chatin and Gary Hirsch. With no rival marque or outfit to beat, the class result was always going to be a question of which of the team's own crews had the better weekend.

Friday morning was wet and then drying, and all three cars led the class at some point. Lecuyer set the quickest PC time, but on his next lap he ran too deep into Variante Villeneuve and left the #47 stranded in the gravel, which put yellow flags out for the closing minutes. The dry afternoon session told more. Chatin was comfortably quickest in class throughout and ended on 1:40.037, eighth overall. He said the car had been unstable in the morning because of a slow puncture the crew had not noticed, and that by the afternoon it was working the tyres at their best.

chapters.title: Hirsch almost two and a half seconds clear
text: The PC drivers all left their runs until the final two laps. Hirsch made the better use of them, setting the class pole with a 1:39.222 on his penultimate lap, a time that was also tenth fastest overall and ahead of the slowest of the LMP2 cars. Lecuyer and Pons were both in the low 1:42s at that stage. Lecuyer improved to 1:41.708 on his last lap and Pons to 1:42.093, which put the #47 second in class and the #48 third, with Hirsch's margin standing at nearly two and a half seconds.

Pons's time was slow enough that the #48 lined up behind the two fastest GTE cars as well as the LMP2 field. Earlier in the session Lecuyer had spun just before the finish line, leaving that part of the track under yellow flags for several minutes.

chapters.title: Hirsch sets the pace
text: Hirsch ran a solid opening stint in the #49 and handed Chatin a good lead at the first stop, a gap Chatin said he set out to keep rather than extend. Elsewhere in the class it was less tidy, as Lecuyer and Pons both spun during their stints. After the driver changes Ayari took the #48 up into second place, and from there the PC cars rarely saw one another on track. The race ran without a safety car, with the few incidents cleared under waved yellows.

chapters.title: A safe run to the flag
text: The rest of the race was a management exercise. Chatin's stated aim was a safe win rather than an extra tenth, because there is little run-off at Imola and the kerbs punish risks. The #49 never lost the lead, and the order behind it, with Ayari ahead of the #47, stayed as it was.

chapters.title: Chatin brings it home
text: Chatin took the flag in the #49 on 103 laps, seventh overall and five laps behind the overall winner. The #48 and #47 both finished on 102 laps, a lap down on their team-mates and six laps behind the overall winner, with Pons and Ayari ahead on the road.

chapters.title: Hirsch and Chatin take the class
text: Hirsch and Chatin won LMPC, with Pons and Ayari second and Loan and Lecuyer third, a lap behind on 102 laps. The class fastest lap went to Chatin, a 1:40.250. He said afterwards that the car's balance had been very good and that he hoped to return to Imola the following year.
The next round of the series was the 3 Hours of Red Bull Ring on 20 July.

facts.v: Hirsch's 1:39.222 was 2.486 seconds quicker than the next PC time, Lecuyer's 1:41.708.

LMGTE.title: RAM Racing's Ferrari wins LMGTE and completes a 1-2-3
LMGTE.dek: Matt Griffin and Johnny Mowlem won from pole by a lap for RAM Racing's first victory, in a Ferrari sweep of the podium decided by 1.8 seconds between AF Corse and RAM's sister car.

chapters.title: Eight cars and a stand-in
text: LMGTE came to Imola with eight cars: Ferrari 458 Italias from RAM Racing (#52, #53), AF Corse (#54, #55) and JMW (#66), and Porsche 911 GT3 RSRs from Proton, IMSA Performance Matmut and Prospeed. At the wet Silverstone opener Proton's Porsche had won the class, with RAM's #52 of Johnny Mowlem and Matt Griffin second, and RAM had taken pole there. Patrick Long replaced Wolf Henzler alongside Patrice Milesi at IMSA Performance, and Prospeed's Perrodo and Crubilé ran without Collard, who was away on Nürburgring 24 Hours duty.

Friday's first session was wet and then drying. Frank Montecalvo, new to the circuit, led the GTE cars early on from Griffin, until Roda and Long made it a Porsche 1-2 in the 2:02s. Griffin took the best time back before handing over to Mowlem. JMW then put Andrea Bertolini into the #66 on cold intermediates, since tyre warmers are banned in the series, and he went to 1:48.583, quickest in the class at the flag and eighth overall. The dry second session was a better guide. Griffin topped it with a 1:43.5, a tenth clear of Bertolini, with the IMSA Porsche and the second RAM car next.

chapters.title: Griffin beats Long by a tenth
text: Long set the early benchmark in the #67 with a 1:42.055 while Griffin was recovering from a spin into the gravel, which brought out the red flag. The lost time was added back and Griffin got his chance. He said he had been on for a time in the mid 1:42s when he took too much kerb at the last corner and ran onto the Astroturf, and that he went out again knowing he had to deliver. His 1:41.994 was the pole, less than a tenth ahead of Long, who had already returned to the pits.

Gunnar Jeannette put the second RAM Ferrari, the #53, third on the class grid with 1:42.669, with Joël Camathias fourth for JMW on 1:42.911. Yannick Mallegol's #54 was fifth on 1:43.551, followed by Perazzini's #55, Ried's #77 and, last of the class, Crubilé's #75 on 1:46.358.

chapters.title: Griffin and Long nose to tail
text: From the start Griffin led Long, the two running nose to tail through the first stint and clouting kerbs side by side without ever coming to blows. Jeannette ran third and unchallenged, easing away from Camathias's JMW. Griffin ran the fuel too long, and the Ferrari coughed halfway round a lap near the end of his stint. He backed off and turned the engine map down, and Long went ahead on his in-lap.

Around the end of the first hour Montecalvo took over the #53 with a lead of 21 seconds over the JMW, and Griffin stayed in the #52 on a full tank. Once Milesi replaced Long in the IMSA Porsche the car dropped back through the order, and it was soon a Ferrari 1-2-3.

chapters.title: Leo and Cioci close in
text: Bertolini lost 45 seconds in the JMW through an incident, which let Montecalvo and Leo back past. Leo then closed on Montecalvo and took second when the American ran through the gravel at a slightly greasy Villeneuve after spots of rain. Montecalvo stayed with the AF Corse car and fought Cioci again in the final minutes. Under pressure he made another small error across the kerbs and Cioci got through, which left RAM bookmarking the podium.

chapters.title: A lap clear
text: Griffin and Mowlem's #52 took the flag on 102 laps, a full lap ahead of the next car. The fight for second ended with AF Corse's #55 and RAM's #53 only 1.8 seconds apart.

chapters.title: RAM's first win
text: Mowlem and Griffin gave RAM Racing its first victory, with Perazzini, Cioci and Leo second for AF Corse and Jeannette and Montecalvo third, so Ferrari took all three places. Bertolini and Camathias were fourth for JMW, followed by Ried, Roda and Ruberti's Proton Porsche, all on 101 laps, while Milesi and Long were sixth, two laps down on the winners. AF Corse's #54 of Mallegol, Bachelier and Blank finished seventh, five laps behind, and Prospeed's Porsche was not classified after 43 laps.

Mowlem said the team had beaten strong opposition, praised the Michelin tyres, and noted that he had done most of the driving at Silverstone while Griffin did it here. The next round was the 3 Hours of Red Bull Ring on 20 July.

facts.v: Griffin's 1:41.994 was less than a tenth of a second quicker than Long's 1:42.055 in the IMSA Porsche, after a spin had brought out a red flag.

GTC.title: SMP Racing's Ferrari wins GTC as Kox is not classified
GTC.dek: Babini, Shaitar and Ladygin won GTC by a lap for SMP Racing's first ELMS victory, while pole-sitter Kox's Lamborghini was not classified after 97 laps.

chapters.title: A class grows to seven
text: GTC, the class for GT3 cars, arrived at Imola much bigger than at Silverstone: seven cars were entered. SMP Racing accounted for most of the newcomers with three Ferrari 458 Italia GT3s, the #68, #69 and #72, in matching liveries. Serguey Zlobin, who shared the #72 with Maurizio Mediani and Boris Rotenberg, said the team was new and had Le Mans in its plans for the following year, although its main programme that season was the Blancpain series, and that racing under the Le Mans banner was a step on the way as well as a chance to get the Ferrari and Le Mans names into Russian media.

The other new name was Kox Racing, which ran a Lamborghini Gallardo LP600 GT3 for Peter Kox and Nico Pronk. Kox explained that running under his own name was meant to make clear which entries carried Lamborghini factory input and which were customer programmes. AF Corse's #62 Ferrari, which had finished 13th overall at Silverstone, was back. Ecurie Ecosse's BMW Z4 GT3 and the Momo Megatron DF1 Audi R8 LMS completed the entry.

In the wet opening session the GT3 cars were faster than the GTEs, and Shaitar emerged well ahead in the final ten minutes with a 1:53.079, with only the Ecosse BMW within two seconds. In the dry afternoon Kox led with a 1:45.108 before getting down into the 1:44s, with the #62 and #72 half a second off his time.

chapters.title: Kox takes pole
text: Kox set the pole with a 1:43.752 in the Lamborghini, which also put him ahead of three GTE cars on the grid. The car had been adjusted overnight and again during the session. Gai was second in the #62 on 1:44.235, half a second back, despite a vicious spin under braking for Acque Minerale.

The rest of the class was more than two seconds off. Giermaziak put the Momo Megatron Audi third on 1:45.786, narrowly ahead of Smith in the Ecosse BMW on 1:45.831, with Shaitar fifth for SMP on 1:46.149. Evstigneev's 1:49.733 in the #68 was the slowest time in the class, and the third SMP car, the #72, did not figure in the timed order at all.

chapters.title: Ladygin gains two places
text: Kox and Gai led away, and Ladygin moved the #69 from fifth in the class to third on the first lap. He chose to consolidate there, following the class leaders and working on his lap times. Kox led the class and ran on the tail of the GTE Ferraris in the opening laps.

At the first stops Gai, Kox and Ladygin came in. Pronk took over the Lamborghini and quickly gave way to Mediani's #72, and when Shaitar took over the #69 he also passed Pronk easily. The Ecosse BMW stopped about 50 minutes in for Smith to hand over to Twyman.

chapters.title: Kox pushing to hold on
text: Kox said he still had to push hard to keep third place when he returned to the Lamborghini for the closing stint. Millroy took over the Ecosse BMW at the end and drove a consistent final stint.

chapters.title: SMP wins by a lap
text: The SMP Racing #69 took the flag on 100 laps, a full lap ahead of AF Corse's #62 on 99. Ecosse's BMW completed 97 laps for third. The #72 SMP Ferrari also finished on 97, with the #68 fifth on 96. The Kox Lamborghini completed 97 laps but was not classified, and the Momo Megatron Audi was not classified after 60.

chapters.title: A first ELMS win for SMP
text: Babini, Shaitar and Ladygin gave SMP Racing its first ELMS victory, with Rizzoli, Gai and Casé second for AF Corse and Millroy, Smith and Twyman third for Ecurie Ecosse. Mediani, Zlobin and Rotenberg were fourth in the #72, ahead of Markozov, Evstigneev and Frolov in the #68. Kox and Pronk were not classified despite completing 97 laps, the same distance as the BMW and the #72, and Bader, Derdaele and Giermaziak's Audi was not classified after 60 laps.
Shaitar said he had always wanted to race at Imola and was delighted to win there. The next round was the 3 Hours of Red Bull Ring on 20 July.

facts.t: Kox pole by half a second
facts.v: Kox's 1:43.752 put the Lamborghini 0.483 seconds clear of Gai's AF Corse Ferrari in GTC qualifying.

facts.v: The win for the #69 was the first ELMS race victory for SMP Racing, a team new to the series at Imola.

facts.v: Kox said the team had calculated Pronk's required driving time too short and that Pronk was held at the pit-lane exit near the end, so the car lost its third place.
The Ecurie Ecosse BMW was penalised for pit-lane speeding but recovered to finish third in class with Millroy in the closing stint.
